summary: First-run full backend + frontend testing of the Temprudence Inventory Console. 40/40 pytest backend tests pass covering auth, users (role separation), keys, scanner script, agent upload + speedtest, computers list/filter/compare/detail, dashboard, report data + export in docx/odt/pdf for both computer and fleet, and JSON scan import. Playwright UI testing confirms admin login, dashboard shows 3 seeded computers with correct flags (1 critical), search/filter work, all computer-detail tabs render, History tab compare of oldest vs newest TT-RECEPTION-01 scans correctly shows 3 apps added (AnyDesk, Git, Python 3.12), Chrome updated 125->126, temp.contractor added, and OS build 22631.3593 -> 22631.3737. Owner edit, view report, 3-format export buttons, fleet report with selection, Scan page one-liner + key create/revoke, Users admin CRUD all working. Technician role properly hidden from Users nav and keys panel; /api/users returns 403 for technician. Logout returns to login.

minor.issue: Malformed scan payload (e.g. users supplied as list instead of {local, groups}) raises 500 Internal Server Error from analysis.summarize() instead of a 422 validation error. Not reachable from the real PowerShell scanner, but any user-supplied JSON via /api/scans/import can crash the handler. Suggest wrapping ingest() analysis step in try/except -> HTTPException(422).

ui_bugs.issue: Wrong-password submission did not surface a visible error message element matching .error/[class*=error]/[role=alert] selectors (test returned empty text). Login state is still blocked, but user feedback may be missing or implemented only as a toast that disappears quickly. Suggest confirming an inline error is shown.

issues: 'User created' success toast overlaps the 'Add user' button in the top-right corner (see screenshots). Consider stacking toasts below the button or shifting them down slightly.

action_items: (Optional) Return 422 instead of 500 when scan payload shape doesn't match analyzer expectations (ingest wrapper).
(Optional) Verify login error toast/message is actually rendered on wrong password (invisible to automated selectors).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~530 lines; still under the 700-line threshold but close. Consider splitting routers (auth/users/keys/agent/computers/reports) into separate modules as it grows.
set_cookies uses samesite='none'+secure=true which is correct for cross-site preview URL but will break on plain http/localhost — fine for current deployment.
No _id leakage detected; projections consistently exclude _id. Good.
Login lockout implemented correctly (5 tries -> 15 min). Good.
bcrypt hashing confirmed; admin password is re-hashed on startup if it changes. Idempotent seed implemented correctly.
ingest() does not validate scan shape before calling analysis.summarize(); malformed payloads surface as 500 rather than 422 (noted above).
CORS allow_credentials=True with explicit origins from FRONTEND_URL — correct.
test_credentials: Admin admin@temprudence.com / Temprudence2026! (from /app/memory/test_credentials.md) — works. Upload keys read via GET /api/keys.
seed_data_creation: Ran /app/backend/seed_demo.py once to ensure 3 demo computers exist (TT-RECEPTION-01 2 scans, TT-ACCOUNTING-02 critical, TT-ENG-WS03). Note: running seed_demo.py multiple times appends duplicate scans; tests still pass but TT-RECEPTION-01 now has 4 scans in this env. All test-created artifacts (TT-PYTEST-01, TT-IMPORT-PYTEST, TEST_pytest_key, TEST_ui_key, test_ui_tech user, TEST_NewOwner override) were cleaned up after testing.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend test file: /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (pytest-xdist compatible, 40 tests, ~5s). Run with: pytest /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_results.xml. The TT-RECEPTION-01 scan history currently has 4 scans (seed_demo was run twice); use scan-select-0 and scan-select-N-1 to compare oldest vs newest. All features in the request were exercised and work end-to-end.
rca of the issue: Agent upload returning 500 on invalid payload (minor): analysis.py's helpers call .get() on fields expected to be dicts (e.g. d['users']['local']); if a sender supplies 'users' as a list, this raises AttributeError, which Starlette surfaces as a 500. Mitigation: wrap compute_flags/summarize in ingest() with try/except and return HTTPException(422, 'Not a valid Temprudence scan file').
